title: review: H7 fix round 3: the flaky rerun gate honours [daemon].flaky_rerun_max (len(runs) < rerun_max, not min(1, rerun_max)); a test with rerun_max = 2 performs two reruns before escalating (review T-0416)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain b9c2972, fb696ce, 4a605cc and a398092 (T-0364, T-0412, T-0414) in git log; never drop or amend them.
Review T-0416 on T-0414, one med finding: orchestrator/daemon.py:151 failure_kind gates the flaky rerun with len(runs) < min(1, rerun_max), which is 1 for every rerun_max at least 1, so raising [daemon].flaky_rerun_max has no effect; only 0 (disable) changes behaviour. Fix: use len(runs) < rerun_max (0 still disables). Test: tests/test_daemon.py::test_flaky_rerun_max_two_reruns_twice_then_escalates (rerun_max 2: a test that fails on both reruns is rerun exactly twice, recorded in resume_hint, then escalated; rerun_max 0: no rerun). Keep test_flaky_rerun_then_escalate (rerun_max 1) and the other T-0364 lineage tests green. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0, then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows a398092, 4a605cc, fb696ce and b9c2972 below your commit
tests/test_daemon.py::test_flaky_rerun_max_two_reruns_twice_then_escalates passes and grep shows no min(1, in the rerun gate
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: _test_ids() extracts `\S+` tokens from untrusted test-failure text with no shape validation, and this diff is the first place that output reaches subprocess.run(['pytest'/'unittest', ...ids], cwd=worktree). A crafted failure line (e.g. from a test file written by an executor that followed an injected instruction from external ticket/web content) could yield a token like '--rootdir=/' and get passed as a real CLI argument to the test runner — argument injection into the rerun subprocess. Validate that each id looks like an actual node id ('::' or a .py path) and reject anything starting with '-' before using it as argv.

_flaky_rerun_command decides pytest-vs-unittest via importlib.util.find_spec('pytest') against the daemon's own interpreter, but the gate that produced the failing ids (tests-green.sh) resolves pytest via `uv run --project .` scoped to the worktree. When those two environments diverge, ids come back in pytest node-id syntax ('a/b.py::test') but the fallback runs `python -m unittest a/b.py::test`, which can't parse that id — the rerun always errors, so a truly flaky test is permanently misclassified as code_defect and never gets marked flaky.
